Tokens act as digital keys that replace traditional session management, offering a more scalable and efficient solution. Access Tokens provide temporary access, while Refresh Tokens enable the issuance of new Access Tokens without requiring users to log in again. The article outlines their differences in purpose, lifespan, storage, and sensitivity to enhance understanding of their functionalities.

Hey there! If you've ever logged into an app or website and it just works without asking you to log in again every 10 minutes, you’ve already met tokens—even if you didn’t know it. Today, we’re going to unwrap this little mystery box and talk about Access Tokens and Refresh Tokens, two smart tools that help modern apps work smoothly and securely.

Let’s get into it—from the basics all the way up to real-world applications.

## What is a Token (And Why Should We Care)?

A token is like a digital key or pass that lets you access something. Think of it as a temporary ID card that says:

> "Hey! I’m allowed to be here because I’ve already shown my ID (like my
>   username and password)."

#### So... Why Do We Need It?

Because typing your password every 5 seconds is:

1. Super annoying
2. Not secure if someone else sees you doing it

Instead of asking you to log in every time, a token takes over and says,
“Relax! I’ve got this.”

## A Little History: What Came Before Tokens?

Back in the day (think early web days), websites mostly used sessions and cookies to remember who you were. When you logged in:

- The server would create a “session” for you.
- It gave you a cookie (not the edible one) with a session ID.
- This cookie was sent back and forth every time you clicked something.

#### It worked, but it had problems:

- It only worked well with websites (not mobile apps or APIs).
- It needed the server to remember every single user’s session (hello, memory overload!).
- It wasn’t very scalable for modern apps or microservices.

## Enter Tokens: A Smarter, Lighter Solution

Modern apps needed something faster, more secure, and easy to scale.

That’s where tokens stepped in. Around the time OAuth 2.0 (an authorization framework) became popular, tokens became the new cool kids on the block. Instead of storing session data on the server, we started using stateless tokens—which means all the info needed is inside the token itself.

## Access Token – Your Instant Pass

An Access Token is like a movie ticket . You show it, and the system lets you in.

#### What’s Inside an Access Token?

It’s usually a string of letters and numbers (or a JWT – JSON Web Token) that includes:

- Who you are (user ID, roles)
- What you’re allowed to do (permissions)
- When the token expires (very important!)

#### But Wait, It Expires?

Yes—and that’s a good thing! Access Tokens are short-lived for security reasons. If someone steals your token, they only get temporary access.

#### Refresh Token – Your Secret Weapon

Now here’s the twist: when the Access Token expires, do you really want the user to log in again?

Nope. That’s where the Refresh Token comes in.

#### What Does It Do?

It’s a longer-lived token that’s only used to get a new Access Token.
So when your Access Token expires:

- Your app says, “Hey, I’ve got this Refresh Token.”
- It sends it to the server.
- The server checks it and sends back a fresh new Access Token.

And boom—no re-login needed.

#### Access Token vs Refresh Token – What’s the Difference?

| Feature         | Access Token                | Refresh Token                 |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |
| Purpose         | Access protected resources  | Get new access tokens         |
| Lifespan        | Short (minutes)             | Long (days or more)           |
| Stored where?   | Client-side (e.g., browser) | Secure place (e.g.,           | HTTP-only cookie) |
| Used how?       | Sent on every API request   | Sent only when token expires  |
| More sensitive? | Not too much                | Yes – needs better protection |
Against the Power: The Power Has Engulfed the Man

The phrase “against the power, the power has engulfed the man” reflects a profound observation about the nature of power and its influence over human beings. Power, in its myriad forms, has been a central theme in philosophical discourses, political theories, and spiritual teachings throughout history. It often manifests as an external force that individuals resist or strive to control, yet, paradoxically, it has the potential to subsume those who engage with it, whether in opposition or in pursuit.

The phrase “against the power, the power has engulfed the man” reflects a profound observation about the nature of power and its influence over human beings. Power, in its myriad forms, has been a central theme in philosophical discourses, political theories, and spiritual teachings throughout history. It often manifests as an external force that individuals resist or strive to control, yet, paradoxically, it has the potential to subsume those who engage with it, whether in opposition or in pursuit.

## The Paradox of Power

Power, as described by sociologists like Max Weber, is the ability to impose one’s will despite resistance. Inherent in this definition is a struggle — a dynamic tension between the individual and the structures or entities that hold power. The act of resisting power can ironically entangle an individual within the very systems they oppose. Michel Foucault, in his exploration of power relations, posited that power is not merely repressive but productive; it shapes identities, discourses, and social practices. Thus, engaging with power transforms both the individual and the system, often leading to an unintended assimilation into the mechanisms of power.

## Philosophical Reflections

Philosophical traditions have long grappled with the dual nature of power. Friedrich Nietzsche, for instance, discussed the “will to power” as a fundamental drive intrinsic to human existence. While this drive can be a source of creativity and growth, it also has the potential to corrupt and consume. Lord Acton’s adage, “Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely,” underscores the moral peril associated with power. Resistance to power, if not grounded in ethical vigilance, risks becoming a mirror image of the oppression it seeks to dismantle.

## Insights from the Bhagavad Gita

The Bhagavad Gita provides a spiritual perspective on the interaction between power and the individual. Arjuna’s internal struggle on the battlefield of Kurukshetra is emblematic of the human confrontation with power, duty, and moral dilemmas. Lord Krishna’s teachings emphasize detachment from the fruits of action (Karma Yoga) and the importance of aligning one’s actions with Dharma (righteousness). This detachment serves as a safeguard against being engulfed by power, as it shifts focus from personal ambition or resistance to a higher, selfless purpose.

In the Gita, Krishna’s guidance suggests that the individual who is anchored in self-awareness and ethical principles can engage with power without being consumed by it. This principle resonates with the idea that true strength lies not in overpowering others but in mastering oneself.

## Psychological Perspectives

Modern psychology also offers insights into the dynamics of power. Social psychologist Philip Zimbardo’s Stanford Prison Experiment revealed how power dynamics can drastically alter human behavior. When individuals are placed in positions of authority or subjugation, their actions often reflect the roles they inhabit, rather than their intrinsic character. This experiment underscores how power can engulf individuals, transforming them into agents of systemic behavior, often beyond their conscious intent.

Similarly, Carl Jung’s concept of the “shadow” highlights the unconscious aspects of the psyche that can dominate when unchecked. Resistance to power without self-awareness can awaken an individual’s shadow, leading to a projection of internal conflicts onto external structures, further entrenching the individual in the dynamics of power.

## Historical and Political Contexts

History provides numerous examples of individuals and movements that, in resisting power, became engulfed by it. Revolutionary leaders, such as Robespierre during the French Revolution, began with ideals of liberty and equality but succumbed to authoritarian tendencies once in power. The cyclical nature of revolutions often illustrates how the act of opposing power can replicate its structures in new forms.

Similarly, the Cold War’s ideological battle between capitalism and communism revealed how each system, in resisting the other, adopted traits of its adversary. Surveillance, propaganda, and militarization became shared tools, blurring the lines between opposition and assimilation.

## Lessons and Pathways Forward

To resist power without being engulfed by it requires a nuanced approach rooted in self-awareness, ethical principles, and a commitment to systemic change rather than personal gain. The teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, alongside insights from psychology and philosophy, emphasize the importance of balancing action with introspection. As individuals and societies engage with power, they must remain vigilant against the seductive allure of control and the insidious ways in which power can reshape intentions.

By recognizing the dual nature of power and grounding resistance in higher values, humanity can aspire to a model of engagement that transcends the cyclical traps of domination and subjugation. In doing so, we honor the timeless wisdom of thinkers and spiritual guides who remind us that true power lies not in conquest but in understanding and harmony.
Are You Using AI as a Crutch or Becoming a Slave to It?
AI (Artificial Intelligence) was designed to replicate human intelligence. It hasn’t reached full human-level thinking yet, but it’s closing the gap faster than we ever imagined.

AI (Artificial Intelligence) was designed to replicate human intelligence. It hasn’t reached full human-level thinking yet, but it’s closing the gap faster than we ever imagined.

Its processing power is far beyond that of the average person, especially in areas involving repetitive tasks. In software, content creation, research, and other digital fields, AI is taking over more and more. And while this brings massive benefits, it also poses a subtle but serious risk.

I’ve seen many of my peers use AI tools to speed up their work. On the surface, it seems efficient. They believe they’re just saving time — automating simple tasks, organizing thoughts, or summarizing readings. But beneath that convenience, something more concerning is happening: they’re slowly replacing their ability to think, search, and learn independently.

Instead of reading through articles or exploring various sources, many now rely entirely on AI to give them instant answers. Assignments meant to help them understand a topic deeply are completed with just a few clicks. They often say, “I’ll read it later,” but in reality, that rarely happens — especially when deadlines are tight and distractions are everywhere.

The truth is, it’s not just about finishing the work. It’s about growing through the process — understanding the material, making mistakes, and building your own cognitive muscle. And that growth is being lost.

## AI Should Support Learning, Not Replace It

I believe the creators of AI intended it to reduce repetitive effort — not to eliminate the human learning curve.

AI can be a powerful educational tool. It can help break down complex topics, suggest learning resources, or give feedback. But if you’re using it just to avoid the effort of reading, researching, or thinking for yourself, you’re undermining your own potential.

For example, when you ask AI to give you bullet points instead of reading a full article, you’re skipping a valuable exercise. You’re avoiding the mental work of identifying key ideas, summarizing them in your own words, and connecting them to your existing knowledge. Over time, this habit weakens your ability to think critically and learn deeply.

Yes, AI is fast. Yes, it’s powerful. But if you rely on power that you haven’t earned — that you don’t fully understand — it can become your weakness.

## What Happens When AI Becomes Better Than You?

Imagine this: you’re using AI to complete tasks at work. You’re praised for efficiency. But as AI keeps evolving, what happens when it can do your job even better — without your help?

At that point, what’s your value?

If you haven’t developed the thinking, problem-solving, and creative skills that AI can’t replicate, you might find yourself replaceable.

That’s the hard truth. And it’s already happening.

## Don’t Be a Slave to the Tool

Use AI as a tool — not a crutch. Let it enhance your learning, not replace it. Let it support your creativity, not do the work for you.

Learning takes time. Thinking deeply is uncomfortable. But that discomfort is what shapes you. It builds the mental strength and adaptability that machines still can’t match.

If you give that up for speed and convenience, you’re not just skipping a step — you’re handing over your growth to something else. And once that becomes the norm, you risk becoming irrelevant in your own life and career.

Build your own mind. Use the machine — don’t become one.

Be Changing, Evolving, Mutating: Embracing the Philosophical Journey of Transformation

In the tapestry of life, change is not merely a passage; it is the very thread that weaves together progress, growth, and innovation. From the ancient wisdom of philosophers to modern scientific understanding, the concepts of change, evolution, and mutation resonate deeply, offering profound insights into the nature of existence and progress. As we navigate the complexities of a rapidly shifting world, these timeless ideas continue to shape how we adapt, evolve, and embrace the unpredictable.

In the tapestry of life, change is not merely a passage; it is the very thread that weaves together progress, growth, and innovation. From the ancient wisdom of philosophers to modern scientific understanding, the concepts of change, evolution, and mutation resonate deeply, offering profound insights into the nature of existence and progress. As we navigate the complexities of a rapidly shifting world, these timeless ideas continue to shape how we adapt, evolve, and embrace the unpredictable.

## Philosophical Foundations of Change

Philosophers across centuries have grappled with the idea of change. Heraclitus, the pre-Socratic thinker, famously declared, “The only constant in life is change.” This notion suggests that change is not a fleeting occurrence but an intrinsic aspect of existence itself — a fundamental principle that governs reality. Similarly, Nietzsche’s idea of eternal recurrence challenges us to embrace change as a necessary cycle of life, urging us to create our own values and truths amidst constant transformation.

Aristotle, in his quest for understanding purpose, or telos, saw change as a means to reach one’s fullest potential. For Aristotle, the process of change is not random but directed, guided by nature’s inherent drive toward improvement. Thus, change is not just inevitable but purposeful — an essential step in the journey toward self-realization and deeper understanding.

## Evolution: A Journey of Adaptation

The idea of evolution, deeply rooted in biology and philosophy, echoes through the ages. Charles Darwin’s theory of natural selection emphasized survival through adaptation, stating, “It is not the strongest of the species that survive, nor the most intelligent, but the one most responsive to change.” This perspective underscores the importance of flexibility and adaptability in shaping the future.

In a similar vein, the concept of evolution has been mirrored in other disciplines. Martin Heidegger, in his existential philosophy, speaks of “being-toward-death,” suggesting that the experience of transformation is integral to understanding existence. Evolution, then, is not just a biological process but a philosophical one — a continual unfolding toward deeper understanding and transformation.

## Mutation: Embracing the Unpredictable

Mutation, often seen as a disruption, introduces elements of unpredictability into both nature and human experience. Yet, great thinkers have recognized its significance. Albert Einstein once said, “In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.” This perspective views mutation as a source of creative potential, where unpredictability can lead to breakthroughs and innovations that defy traditional boundaries.

Friedrich Nietzsche’s notion of amor fati, or “love of fate,” aligns with this unpredictability. He argued for embracing the chaotic, unforeseen changes of life as opportunities for growth. Mutation, therefore, becomes a catalyst for radical change, pushing the boundaries of what is possible.

## The Role of Adaptation in a Constantly Shifting World

In today’s fast-paced world, adaptation has become an imperative for survival and growth. As Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi highlights in his research on flow states, “Adaptability is the key to mastering the challenges of change.” Embracing uncertainty, navigating complexity, and evolving with purpose are crucial for individuals and organizations alike.

Psychological safety, as championed by Dr. Amy Edmondson, plays a significant role in fostering environments where change is welcomed rather than resisted. In such spaces, individuals can innovate freely, knowing that mistakes and transformations are part of the natural evolution of ideas.

## Conclusion

The journey of change, evolution, and mutation is deeply embedded in the philosophies of our greatest thinkers. From Heraclitus to Nietzsche, from Darwin to Heidegger, these ideas serve as guiding lights in a world marked by constant flux. Embracing change as a pathway toward deeper understanding and adaptation as a way to thrive offers not just resilience but the opportunity for meaningful progress. In doing so, we align ourselves with the very essence of existence — a perpetual evolution toward what could be.

## 1. Creator is Not Just a Word
“Creator” is not like a word such as potato, which is used everywhere. It is often thrown around casually, but at its core, being a creator is about skill, mastery, and intrinsic motivation.

Psychology research shows that intrinsic motivation, doing something because it is inherently satisfying rather than for external rewards is a strong predictor of creativity and long-term engagement. If you are a creator, it means you are someone who is motivated to develop and express your specialized skills and share them with others.

## 2. Sharing Your Work

Creation is one part; sharing is another. The internet provides platforms to showcase your work:

Videos: platforms like YouTube or Instagram, depending on the content duration.
Visual graphics: LinkedIn, Dribbble, Twitter, Instagram, depending on your audience and type of content.
The platform affects reach, engagement, and growth, but your motivation should remain internal rather than platform-driven.

## 3. The Algorithm Factor

Algorithms on social media are designed to maximize user engagement and ad revenue, not necessarily to support creators. Research in neuroscience shows that dopamine, a neurotransmitter linked to reward, spikes when we receive likes, comments, or new followers. This creates a feedback loop where creators may experience temporary pleasure, but also anxiety or frustration when engagement drops.

Understanding this helps maintain intrinsic motivation rather than becoming dependent on external validation.

## 4. Society and Social Pressure

Humans are social beings, and social comparison is natural. Psychologists have found that comparing oneself to peers can lead to both motivation and negative emotions like envy.

For example, friends may outwardly say, “Go ahead, be a creator,” but inwardly feel envy or doubt. Society often pressures individuals to stick to traditional career paths, making breaking free from the 9-to-5 loop socially challenging. Awareness of these dynamics can help you navigate them without losing focus.

## 5. Doing Extra Work

Being a creator requires managing multiple responsibilities. Cognitive science shows that multitasking and divided attention can increase cognitive load and stress. You are effectively doing extra work:

Your job to sustain income.
Creating additional content (videos, graphics, blogs).
Sharing your work online and engaging with the audience.
This requires discipline, time management, and emotional resilience. You also need social capital, support from friends, family, and your network to sustain this work without burnout.

## 6. Inner Clarity Comes First

To manage work, creation, social life, and personal well-being, you need self-awareness and clarity. Research in psychology shows that people who reflect on their values, goals, and identity experience greater life satisfaction and decision-making quality.

Ask yourself:

Who am I?
What do I want in life?
How do I want to live my life?
Without this, people risk regret and burnout, as unexamined decisions often lead to dissatisfaction later in life. Developing self-awareness first allows you to navigate challenges consciously and intentionally.

## 7. Be Human First

Be human first, then be the doer. Conscious action matters more than mechanical action. Just doing things without reflection makes you part of the algorithmic loop, where your work is shaped more by external forces than by your own purpose.

While being genuine can foster trust and deepen relationships, it can also lead to misunderstandings, discomfort, and even social alienation. Striking the right balance between honest expression and social harmony is a delicate dance, one that has been explored by countless thinkers throughout history.

In a world where social dynamics often prioritize politeness and tact, the virtues of authenticity and straightforwardness are sometimes viewed as disruptive or even harmful. While being genuine can foster trust and deepen relationships, it can also lead to misunderstandings, discomfort, and even social alienation. Striking the right balance between honest expression and social harmony is a delicate dance, one that has been explored by countless thinkers throughout history.

## The Power of Authenticity: Embracing Your True Self

Authenticity is often celebrated as a key to personal growth and deeper connections with others. Carl Rogers, a pioneer in humanistic psychology, believed that being fully authentic allows individuals to experience genuine relationships and self-acceptance. “The curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change,” Rogers said. In this light, authenticity becomes a pathway to self-awareness and personal fulfillment — an act of embracing one’s true nature without fear of judgment.

However, this authenticity can sometimes clash with societal expectations. In relationships, workplaces, or even within family dynamics, straightforwardness can feel abrasive when honesty challenges the status quo or confronts difficult truths. The philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau noted, “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.” This suggests that while authenticity frees us, it also risks isolating us from the very communities we wish to connect with.

## Straightforwardness: Navigating the Fine Line Between Honesty and Harshness

Being straightforward often requires courage. When we choose to speak openly and clearly, it can create moments of clarity and understanding, allowing others to see things from a new perspective. Yet, as Friedrich Nietzsche warned, “Whoever fights monsters should see to it that in the process he does not become a monster.” In this way, straightforwardness can be both a tool for growth and a risk for alienation if it is not tempered by empathy and respect.

In today’s interconnected world, where communication is often mediated by digital platforms and social norms, straightforwardness can easily be misinterpreted or taken out of context. What is meant as honest feedback may be perceived as criticism, causing harm to relationships that require nuance and sensitivity.

## The Risks of Over-Authenticity: When Straightforwardness Becomes Harmful

While authenticity is a cornerstone of meaningful interactions, unfiltered honesty can sometimes lead to unintended consequences. Excessive straightforwardness can come across as blunt or insensitive, particularly when it fails to consider the emotional well-being of others. Social philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that “The human condition is one of powerlessness, and this powerlessness creates a need for the protection of self-esteem.” Thus, while honesty is valued, its delivery must be balanced with compassion.

In professional settings, especially, straightforwardness can lead to friction and even conflict if it challenges authority or defies organizational norms. Moreover, in personal relationships, expressing thoughts without tact may result in strained connections or the erosion of trust, even if intentions were purely constructive.

## Authenticity and Straightforwardness: A Balancing Act

Striking the right balance between authenticity and straightforwardness requires mindfulness and emotional intelligence. Aristotle’s concept of phronesis, or practical wisdom, serves as a guide here — balancing reason, experience, and compassion in decision-making. Being authentic involves embracing one’s true self, but doing so in a way that respects others’ boundaries and acknowledges social context.

In our increasingly complex world, where individualism clashes with communal expectations, this balance is more crucial than ever. It is not enough to be honest; we must also consider how our honesty contributes to meaningful relationships and a more understanding society.

## Conclusion

Being authentic and straightforward can be powerful tools for personal growth and connection, but they also carry risks when taken too far. As with many virtues, moderation is key. When tempered with empathy, understanding, and a willingness to consider context, authenticity and straightforwardness can create deep, meaningful interactions. However, unchecked, they may cause harm or alienation. In finding the sweet spot between honesty and tact, we navigate the delicate balance of being true to ourselves while fostering harmony in our relationships.

Instead, take a step back and ask yourself:

> “What did I really gain from this? And how have I used it to grow?”

That reflection is worth more than any badge. It’s the proof of learning that no certificate can truly capture.

## When I Turned My Face Off

I hid my profile picture from anyone who wasn’t connected with me.

Borrowed Thought vs. Own Thought: The Critical Difference and Why It Matters

Our minds are constantly influenced by the thoughts, opinions, and ideas we come across, both in personal conversations and in the vast content offered by media, books, and the internet. We’re essentially living in a marketplace of thoughts, where some ideas are bought without question and others are personally crafted and refined. The distinction between borrowed thought and own thought lies at the heart of how we navigate life’s complexities and make choices that align with our true selves. However, the impact of adopting borrowed thoughts without critical examination can be subtle, and it may even turn destructive.

Our minds are constantly influenced by the thoughts, opinions, and ideas we come across, both in personal conversations and in the vast content offered by media, books, and the internet. We’re essentially living in a marketplace of thoughts, where some ideas are bought without question and others are personally crafted and refined. The distinction between borrowed thought and own thought lies at the heart of how we navigate life’s complexities and make choices that align with our true selves. However, the impact of adopting borrowed thoughts without critical examination can be subtle, and it may even turn destructive.

## What is Borrowed Thought?

A borrowed thought is an idea, belief, or perspective that we take from external sources without extensive personal reflection or questioning. It’s something we’ve heard, read, or seen, and it makes sense — at least on the surface. For instance, adopting a popular political opinion, a trending lifestyle choice, or the latest productivity philosophy without fully understanding its implications is an example of borrowing thought.

While adopting others’ ideas can save us time and provide convenient mental shortcuts, relying heavily on borrowed thoughts can carry significant risks if we don’t take the time to examine and validate them.

## What is Own Thought?

An own thought, in contrast, is born from personal reflection, experience, and firsthand reasoning. It’s an idea we have crafted ourselves, aligning with our unique beliefs, values, and life circumstances. It isn’t merely accepted at face value but has been filtered, questioned, and analyzed to see if it stands up to scrutiny. Think of it as a carefully tailored outfit versus an off-the-rack ensemble; the former fits us perfectly, while the latter may need adjustments or may not suit us at all.

## Why Unexamined Borrowed Thoughts Can Be Destructive

Borrowed thoughts become harmful when they are accepted as truths without evaluation. They may shape our decisions, interactions, and self-perceptions, yet be misaligned with our values or circumstances. Here are ways in which unexamined borrowed thoughts can be detrimental:

1. Loss of Individuality and Self-Identity
   Borrowing thoughts mindlessly can lead to a disconnection from our core identity, as we start defining ourselves through others’ ideas rather than discovering our own. Over time, it becomes challenging to distinguish which thoughts are genuinely ours and which are simply reflections of what we’ve absorbed. This loss of individuality can make us feel detached, uncertain, and unfulfilled, as we’re acting on a mental template that doesn’t truly belong to us.

2. Hasty Decision-Making and Regret
   Borrowed thoughts can lead us to adopt actions, attitudes, or opinions that don’t suit us. For instance, social media is filled with trending advice on financial, relational, and lifestyle choices that may not work for everyone. Following advice blindly because it’s popular often leads to regret. Since it wasn’t a decision aligned with our own life goals or context, we may end up with unintended consequences, feeling as though we’ve taken a shortcut only to find ourselves lost.

3. Reinforcement of Bias and Prejudice
   Borrowing thoughts can also reinforce biases and prejudices when we adopt narrow perspectives or views without questioning their validity. Political, social, or cultural biases are often inherited or absorbed from our surroundings and can become deeply ingrained if they go unexamined. These biases can become barriers to seeing other perspectives and developing empathy, stunting our ability to engage with others meaningfully and contributing to societal division.

4. Stagnation of Personal Growth
   Personal growth is about challenging our own beliefs, identifying flaws in our understanding, and striving for a clearer, more nuanced perspective. However, when we lean on borrowed thoughts without scrutiny, we’re not actively engaging with our experiences and insights. By failing to explore and challenge ideas, we deny ourselves the growth that comes from making our own mistakes, adjusting our worldview, and refining our sense of purpose.

## The Role of Critical Thinking in Borrowing Thoughts

Borrowing thoughts isn’t inherently negative. Some of the world’s greatest philosophies, movements, and advancements have come from the sharing of ideas. But before adopting a borrowed thought, it’s essential to filter it through critical thinking and see it from multiple perspectives. Here are steps to do so effectively:

1. Question the Source
   Who or what is the origin of this thought? Consider the reliability, agenda, and context of the source. Even if an idea comes from a respected person or institution, it’s still essential to assess its relevance and appropriateness for your circumstances.

2. Assess Relevance to Your Life
   Ask yourself if the thought aligns with your own values, goals, and experiences. A popular opinion might not suit your unique context. Consider if it would serve you well long-term or if it simply feels attractive in the moment.

3. Explore Contrasting Viewpoints
   Look into differing opinions and perspectives on the topic. Understanding why someone might think differently helps you develop a more balanced viewpoint and identifies blind spots in the borrowed thought that might not align with your broader understanding.

4. Look for Supporting Evidence
   Challenge the thought by searching for data, studies, or historical examples that either validate or dispute it. Does the evidence support the conclusions, or are there flaws in the reasoning? Evidence-based thinking helps avoid the tendency to believe something simply because it “sounds right.”

5. Reflect on Your Own Intuition and Experience
   Think about how this thought feels based on your personal experiences. Sometimes our own instincts can alert us when a borrowed thought doesn’t sit right. Trust your gut feelings as much as your intellect in deciding whether to integrate the thought into your worldview.

## Transforming Borrowed Thoughts into Own Thoughts

When we encounter ideas that resonate with us, they can serve as starting points rather than end points. By critically evaluating and modifying these ideas based on our own experiences, we can transform borrowed thoughts into our own thoughts. Here’s how:

- Personalize the Idea: Adapt the thought to your life by making it relevant to your context and goals. For example, if a productivity technique resonates with you, adjust it to suit your schedule, preferences, and needs rather than following it rigidly.
- Apply and Test: Experiment with the thought in real-life scenarios and observe the outcomes. Testing ideas in practice helps reveal whether they genuinely benefit us or if they need adjustment.
- Review and Revisit: As time goes by, continue to question if the borrowed thought still serves you well. Experiences change, and so should our thoughts. Consistently revisiting and reassessing borrowed ideas can ensure they continue to align with your evolving sense of self.

## Embracing Thought Ownership in a World of Influence

In a society where information and ideas are shared more freely than ever, learning to balance borrowed and own thoughts is essential. Being open to learning from others enriches our understanding of the world, while holding space for our own reflections keeps us authentic and aligned with our true selves.

Borrowed thoughts, when evaluated critically, become tools for insight and innovation. When taken at face value, however, they can limit self-discovery and growth. By cultivating the discipline to scrutinize ideas before adopting them, we can transform our mental landscapes into places of originality and strength — living lives true to ourselves and grounded in our own beliefs and experiences.

Every day, we’re bombarded with thoughts, plans, and distractions. We start the day with a schedule, an intention to be productive, yet often find ourselves doing the complete opposite. This might sound familiar: I had a day planned out, but instead, I watched a movie. After the movie ended, instead of getting back to my scheduled tasks, I drifted to YouTube, scrolling through content in search of either motivation or entertainment.

At one point, I found myself clicking on a video titled “Is the MERN Stack Dead?” — a topic completely irrelevant to my current goal of preparing for an exam. I wasn’t even planning to become a MERN stack developer, but curiosity led me down a rabbit hole. It’s strange how, even when we’re aware of what we should be doing, we often find ourselves sidetracked.

This behavior is fueled by the stories we tell ourselves: “I’ll get to it later; there’s plenty of time.” We delay, convinced we’ll start working after just one more video, one more search. But the reality is, we end up watching irrelevant content, consuming information that doesn’t even align with our long-term goals. Why did I even open YouTube when I had already told myself I would get back to studying after the movie?

The truth is, my “schedule” isn’t real. It exists only on paper. In reality, I make plans but rarely follow them. Instead, I waste time watching motivational videos or intellectual podcasts, tricking myself into thinking I’m being productive. Yes, those videos might provide information or inspiration, but they don’t replace the value of actively working on my goals. I end up consuming content, passively absorbing ideas, instead of diving deep into my own learning and sticking to a plan that would actually help me grow.

The root of the problem? I’ve grown too comfortable. College life is easy — meals are provided, monthly allowances arrive like clockwork, and everything feels safe. But this comfort has led me to forget that soon, college will end. The real world is coming, and I’ll need to figure out how to secure a job, provide for myself, and build the life I want. Yet, instead of focusing on these future goals, I escape into distractions, telling myself I’ll tackle them later.

If you genuinely enjoy something — whether it’s reading, sketching, or coding — you naturally create time for it. You’d set a schedule, update your skills, and actively work towards improvement. But when the task feels hard, or the reward isn’t immediate, we often find excuses. We say we’ll do it later, only to fall into the trap of mindless content consumption. We drift from one random topic to another, often unrelated to our goals, and before we know it, hours have passed with nothing to show for it.

The key is to break this cycle. To stop giving in to distractions and start focusing on what truly matters. It’s not enough to just make plans — you have to act on them. It’s time to stop escaping into the flow of random content and start building the future you want, one deliberate step at a time.

Celebrities: Credible Icons or Misleading Influencers?

In today’s world, celebrities have transcended their traditional roles as entertainers, athletes, and artists. They’ve become influential figures in politics, health advocacy, product endorsements, and even social movements. But the question arises: should celebrities be viewed as indicators of credibility? Examining this issue from multiple perspectives reveals a nuanced and thought-provoking debate.

In today’s world, celebrities have transcended their traditional roles as entertainers, athletes, and artists. They’ve become influential figures in politics, health advocacy, product endorsements, and even social movements. But the question arises: should celebrities be viewed as indicators of credibility? Examining this issue from multiple perspectives reveals a nuanced and thought-provoking debate.

## The Case For Celebrity Credibility

- Massive Reach and Influence: Celebrities have an unparalleled ability to reach millions. When they champion causes — be it climate change, mental health awareness, or public health campaigns — their involvement often garners widespread attention that experts or NGOs may struggle to achieve.
- Personal Stories as Advocacy: Many celebrities share personal experiences that resonate with their audience. For instance, when an actor opens up about battling depression or an athlete discusses their struggle with injuries, it can encourage fans to seek help or follow better practices.
- Expert-Backed Initiatives: In some cases, celebrities collaborate with experts to endorse credible initiatives. For example, campaigns promoting vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic often relied on celebrities to amplify scientifically backed messages.

## The Counterargument: Credibility in Question

- Lack of Expertise: Most celebrities are not subject-matter experts. Endorsements — whether for political candidates, health products, or social issues — can sometimes mislead the public, especially when backed by limited or inaccurate information.
- Commercial Interests: Many celebrity endorsements are driven by profit rather than genuine belief in the product or cause. This blurs the line between advocacy and advertising, making their credibility questionable.
- Overshadowing Real Experts: Celebrity involvement often eclipses the voices of genuine experts. A social media post by a famous actor may receive more attention than a well-researched article by a scientist, leading to skewed public perception.

## The Indian Context: A Growing Dependency on Star Power

In India, the reliance on celebrities as markers of credibility has reached unprecedented levels. From endorsing consumer products to influencing voting patterns, their word often holds more weight than detailed data or nuanced arguments. This phenomenon reflects a broader cultural trend where idolization overrides critical thinking. For example, during elections, a political endorsement by a film star can swing voter behavior, irrespective of the candidate’s actual qualifications.

At the same time, this dependency raises concerns about the decline in public sensibility. Are we as a society increasingly prioritizing charisma over competence? And how do we balance the impact of celebrity culture with the need for informed decision-making?

Striking a Balance
To address this growing issue, several steps can be taken:

- Promoting Media Literacy: Encouraging people to critically analyze information, including celebrity endorsements, can reduce blind trust in star power.
- Elevating Expert Voices: Platforms should prioritize giving space to subject-matter experts alongside celebrity advocates, ensuring a balanced narrative.
- Accountability for Celebrities: Celebrities endorsing products or causes should be held accountable for the accuracy and ethical implications of their messages.

## Conclusion

While celebrities undoubtedly hold immense power to shape public opinion, treating them as sole indicators of credibility can be problematic. As society, we must embrace a more discerning approach, valuing expertise and critical thinking over blind admiration. Only then can we strike a balance between leveraging celebrity influence and fostering a culture of informed sensibility.
Christopher Nolan: The Visionary Director Who Redefined Modern Cinema

Christopher Nolan has become one of the most influential and celebrated directors of the 21st century. Known for his cerebral storytelling, visual innovation, and genre-bending narratives, Nolan’s work redefines the boundaries of mainstream cinema. His films — ranging from superhero sagas and sci-fi epics to psychological thrillers — demonstrate an artistic ambition and philosophical depth that has resonated with both critics and audiences. This article delves into what makes Christopher Nolan a cinematic visionary, exploring the key elements of his unique style, influences, and contributions to modern filmmaking.

Christopher Nolan has become one of the most influential and celebrated directors of the 21st century. Known for his cerebral storytelling, visual innovation, and genre-bending narratives, Nolan’s work redefines the boundaries of mainstream cinema. His films — ranging from superhero sagas and sci-fi epics to psychological thrillers — demonstrate an artistic ambition and philosophical depth that has resonated with both critics and audiences. This article delves into what makes Christopher Nolan a cinematic visionary, exploring the key elements of his unique style, influences, and contributions to modern filmmaking.

## Early Influences and Rise to Fame

Christopher Nolan was born in London in 1970 and began experimenting with film at a young age, making short movies with his father’s Super 8 camera. Influenced by directors like Stanley Kubrick, Ridley Scott, and Andrei Tarkovsky, Nolan’s early fascination with the psychological and the surreal laid the foundation for his future works. He burst onto the independent film scene with Following (1998), a low-budget noir that showcased his ability to craft suspenseful narratives with minimal resources. This debut paved the way for Memento (2000), a groundbreaking thriller told in reverse chronological order, which earned him critical acclaim and established his reputation as a director with a knack for unconventional storytelling.

## Signature Styles and Techniques

Nolan’s films are known for their narrative complexity, stunning visuals, and intense focus on psychological themes. Several signature elements have come to define his style:

1. Nonlinear and Complex Storytelling

One of Nolan’s trademarks is his penchant for non-linear narratives, as seen in Memento, The Prestige (2006), and Inception (2010). These films play with timelines and perspectives, challenging audiences to piece together the story themselves. Nolan’s nonlinear approach allows him to explore themes like memory, perception, and the subjective nature of truth. This emphasis on structure-as-storytelling engages audiences deeply, making them active participants in the narrative rather than passive viewers.

2. Exploration of Time and Reality

Few directors engage with time as intricately as Nolan. His movies like Inception, Interstellar (2014), and Tenet (2020) use time as a plot device and a thematic focal point. In Inception, the layered structure of dreams creates a multi-tiered timeline, while Interstellar delves into time dilation and its emotional ramifications. In Tenet, Nolan takes time manipulation to new heights with “time inversion,” in which events unfold in reverse. This fascination with time and its implications makes Nolan’s work intellectually engaging and invites viewers to consider the fluidity of reality.

3. Realism and Practical Effects

Despite his fondness for sci-fi and fantasy elements, Nolan grounds his films in a sense of realism by favoring practical effects over CGI. For example, in Inception, the rotating hallway scene was filmed with an actual rotating set, and in The Dark Knight (2008), Nolan famously flipped an 18-wheeler truck in downtown Chicago. His commitment to practical effects makes his films feel tangible and immediate, giving even fantastical scenes a weight that CGI often lacks. This dedication to realism not only enhances the viewing experience but also highlights Nolan’s respect for cinema as an art form.

4. Psychological Depth and Moral Complexity

Nolan’s characters are rarely one-dimensional; they often face deep psychological or moral dilemmas. In The Dark Knight trilogy, Batman grapples with the ethics of vigilantism and the nature of heroism, while The Prestige examines the cost of ambition through the story of two rival magicians. Nolan’s protagonists are often flawed, introspective, and willing to confront their darkest selves to achieve their goals. This complexity invites audiences to ponder ethical questions, adding layers of meaning to his films.

5. Collaboration with Key Creatives

Nolan frequently collaborates with a trusted team of creative professionals, including cinematographer Wally Pfister, composer Hans Zimmer, and production designer Nathan Crowley. His partnership with Zimmer, in particular, has yielded some of modern cinema’s most iconic scores, such as the epic “Time” track from Inception and the tension-laden score for Dunkirk (2017). These collaborations enhance the immersive quality of Nolan’s films, blending visuals, music, and atmosphere into a cohesive experience.

## Major Works and Their Impact

1. The Dark Knight Trilogy (2005–2012)

With Batman Begins, The Dark Knight, and The Dark Knight Rises, Nolan reinvented the superhero genre, offering a darker, more grounded interpretation of Batman. The Dark Knight, in particular, became a cultural phenomenon and redefined what superhero movies could be. With its complex villain, the Joker (portrayed by Heath Ledger), and themes of chaos versus order, the film transcended the comic book genre and became a touchstone for modern cinema. The trilogy’s success proved that blockbuster films could be both intellectually stimulating and commercially successful.

2. Inception (2010)

Inception is perhaps Nolan’s most ambitious film to date, weaving a heist movie within a dreamscape. Its layered dream worlds and exploration of consciousness fascinated audiences, making it a cultural and financial success. The film’s iconic “dream within a dream” structure and open-ended finale continue to spark debates and analyses, highlighting Nolan’s ability to create lasting cinematic puzzles. Inception also solidified his reputation as a director capable of blending art with commercial appeal.

3. Interstellar (2014)

In Interstellar, Nolan combined scientific concepts with emotional storytelling, exploring the survival of humanity, the bond between a father and his daughter, and the vastness of space. With its realistic portrayal of black holes and time dilation, the film became notable for its scientific accuracy, even influencing NASA’s research on black hole imaging. The movie’s emotional core, along with its stunning visuals, demonstrated Nolan’s range and cemented his status as a visionary director.

4. Dunkirk (2017)

With Dunkirk, Nolan took a different approach, creating a war film with minimal dialogue and a unique three-part narrative structure. The movie depicts the rescue of Allied soldiers from the beaches of Dunkirk through three perspectives — land, sea, and air — each unfolding over different time spans. This structure, paired with the relentless tension of Zimmer’s score, immerses the audience in the soldiers’ desperation and fear. Dunkirk showcased Nolan’s versatility and earned him his first Oscar nomination for Best Director.

Nolan’s Lasting Legacy in Modern Cinema
Christopher Nolan’s work has left an indelible mark on cinema. He is one of the few directors capable of producing high-concept, artistically ambitious films that also achieve commercial success. By blending spectacle with intellectual rigor, he has raised audience expectations for blockbuster films and redefined what it means to create “mainstream” cinema. His influence is evident in how other directors approach complex narratives, as well as in the growing audience appetite for movies that challenge and provoke.

Beyond his technical and narrative innovations, Nolan’s commitment to practical effects, film over digital, and IMAX technology demonstrates his respect for the craft of filmmaking. His advocacy for the theatrical experience has made him a champion of traditional cinema in an age of digital streaming, fighting to preserve the communal experience of watching films on the big screen.

## Conclusion

Christopher Nolan is more than just a filmmaker; he is a visionary who has transformed contemporary cinema with his dedication to storytelling, visual mastery, and thematic depth. His films invite us to ponder profound questions about time, reality, and the human psyche, often leaving us with as many questions as answers. By continually pushing the boundaries of what cinema can be, Nolan has become one of the defining directors of our time, inspiring both audiences and fellow filmmakers to embrace the power of storytelling in its most ambitious form.

As we look forward to his future works, Nolan’s legacy as a director who reimagines the possibilities of film is already secure. His influence is a testament to the power of imagination, intellect, and a relentless commitment to craft — qualities that ensure his films will be celebrated and studied for generations to come.

Coffee Bot: From Gemini API in Streamlit to FastAPI
Moving Coffeebot from Streamlit to FastAPI

Hello reader, nice to see you back! Today I’m going to talk about a project I originally built using the Gemini API back in Jan, 2025 and how I revamped it into a better version in 2025 using FastAPI and a full frontend stack. ## First, What is an API? Let’s quickly talk about APIs, especially if you are new or just forgot. Imagine you are in a coffee shop. You sit at your table and order a cappuccino by calling the waiter. Now, do you care how the coffee is made? Do you need to know the temperature, sugar ratio, milk amount, cream or coffee beans? Of course not. You just want the cappuccino on your table. The waiter takes care of communicating with the kitchen and bring it to you. That is exactly how API works. It handles the communication between your request(as a user or developer) and the system that actually does the work behind the scenes. For example, when I built a weather website, did I install satellites and sensors all over the world? Nope. I simply used an API provided by the company that already collects and serves that data. My job was just to display it on my website, the rest is handled by the API. ## Jan, 2025: The first version - Gemini API with Streamlit This was my second serious attempt at using an API in a project. I opened up VS Code, wrote a few lines of Python, added some Streamlit for the UI, imported the Gemini modules, and added the API key in the .env file. Since I was ( and still am) a student, I could not afford the pro version. So, I used the free tier model gemini-1.5-flash. I ran a few tests, fixed common bugs like API errors and missing environment variables, and eventually deployed it on Streamlit. That is how Coffee Chatbot was born, my first AI chatbot built using Gemini API. Aug, 2025: The upgrade - FastAPI, React and Tailwind Fast forward to August, 2025 - I had to learn FastAPI. And I thought, “Why not upgrade my old chatbot project from Streamlit to FastAPI?” So, I started rebuilding it from scratch using FastAPI, checking the documentation as I went along. Quick intro if you are new: FastAPI is a modern, high performance Python web framework developed by Sebastian Ramírez ( popular as Tianglo). It is known for its speed and simplicity I built the backend using FastAPI, but unlike Streamlit, which takes care of the frontend, FastAPI is mostly backend-focused. That meant I needed to build a custom frontend. ## Frontend Makeover: React, TypeScript and Tailwind I didn’t want a plain UI with basic HTML/CSS/JavaScript, so I took a leap and built a better UI, something that looked more like ChatGPT or Gemini. Dear Me: Remember, You Are a Traveler

> Dear Me,
>
> You’ve started to forget again.
>
> You’ve begun to drift — lost in the noise, in people, in thoughts that don’t belong to you. So I’m writing this, for you to remember what you already know deep down:
>
> You are a traveler.
>
> You came into this life without a path laid out for you. A clean slate.
> You are free to draw it as you wish.
> Yes, there will be obstacles. Yes, you will stumble.
> But you walk alone — and one day, you will leave alone.
>
> Still, life has a way of making you forget this truth.
> It surrounds you with people, smiles, temporary joys.
> And in those moments, you start to believe you are not alone.
> You start to believe the journey can be paused, delayed, or ignored.
>
> But it can’t.
> You know that.
>
> Remember the girl you liked once in college?
> You said you wanted to be friends — but it was something more.
> Maybe you laughed when you saw her, maybe you smiled like a child.
> But even that was just the forgetfulness of a traveler —
> one who lost himself in the scenery, not the destination.
>
> She, too, is a traveler.
> Just like your parents. Your friends. Everyone.
> They’re all walking their own path —
> alone, just like you —
> and one day, they too will leave when their time comes.
>
> So stop expecting someone to show you the way.
> Stop waiting for someone to walk it for you.
> No one can.
>
> Most people wander endlessly.
> They forget they even have a destination.
> Why?
> Because they never question what they’ve been told.
> They fear that what they believe might be a lie.
> They fear waking up.
>
> But not you.
>
> You’ve glimpsed the truth before:
> Life isn’t a journey.
> It’s a cage.
> A windowless cell disguised with color, noise, and comfort.

>
> So let me remind you:
> You are not here to laugh endlessly,
> to chase smiles that fade,
> to follow crowds that go nowhere.
>
> You are here to complete the journey.
> To reach the destination only your soul remembers.
>
> Stay awake.
> Because one day, you’ll sleep forever.
> And if you don’t complete the journey —

>
> With clarity,
>
> You.

Ego is a subtle derivative of human existence — always present, but not always seen. It can emerge in any situation, and though it often hides beneath the surface, it reveals itself to those who observe carefully.

Consider a simple example: a competition. When you win, your joy may overflow. But that intense, almost uncontrollable feeling — the shouting, the boasting — isn’t just excitement. It’s the ego at work, surging up as a response to being validated, being “better.”

What’s more revealing is what happens when you lose. The ego doesn’t disappear — it shifts. It may lead to disappointment, anger, or a sense that the outcome was unfair. It may nudge you into questioning the judgment, or worse, trigger emotional reactions like group anger or verbal abuse.

What’s important to understand is that these reactions don’t always come from your core self. They are often the result of a disturbed ego — a turbulence of emotion, a storm that clouds your usual behavior.

Unchecked, ego can derail relationships, ruin moments, and distort reality. But when recognized and understood, it becomes something we can manage — even transcend.

In observing our reactions honestly, we create space for self-awareness. And with that awareness comes growth.
Embracing the Quiet Moments: Finding Beauty and Meaning in Solitude

In a world that’s always bustling, where productivity and connectivity are celebrated, solitude is often seen as something to escape from rather than embrace. Yet, there is a unique, almost sacred beauty in the quiet moments spent alone, when the world falls away, and you are left with nothing but your own thoughts, dreams, and sometimes fears.

In a world that’s always bustling, where productivity and connectivity are celebrated, solitude is often seen as something to escape from rather than embrace. Yet, there is a unique, almost sacred beauty in the quiet moments spent alone, when the world falls away, and you are left with nothing but your own thoughts, dreams, and sometimes fears.

When you’re alone, free from external pressures and responsibilities, a true, unfiltered version of yourself begins to surface. You might feel an instinctive urge to be productive, to create something, or to learn, as if driven by an invisible force. On other days, the softer, more indulgent side may emerge, prompting you to dive into comfort, whether by binge-watching a favorite series, scrolling through memories, or simply letting time drift by. In these quiet spaces, the complex tapestry of who you are comes alive.

## The Duality of Alone Time

When we think of solitude, we often imagine a quiet, tranquil experience where we can reflect and recharge. But solitude also brings us face-to-face with parts of ourselves we might not be ready to see. The driven student who meticulously plans every minute during exam season might find themselves, post-exams, drawn to unstructured, even “wasteful” activities. In these moments, our inner selves — both the productive and the indulgent — clash and intermingle, revealing the duality within us.

The pull toward distraction, comfort, and pleasure isn’t a flaw; it’s a natural reaction to sustained periods of pressure and control. Think of it as a balancing act where we’re given the opportunity to fully explore both sides. Structure and spontaneity, drive and ease — each is essential in its way, and it’s through solitude that we begin to understand how these contrasting parts of us fit together.

## Finding Balance Between Discipline and Release

There is power in balance. Too much structure, and we risk burnout; too much indulgence, and our goals can slip away. Alone time offers a delicate opportunity to explore where we sit on that spectrum and, perhaps more importantly, to decide where we’d like to be.

By recognizing when we’re giving in to comfort rather than commitment, we can steer ourselves gently toward a balance that feels fulfilling. It might look like setting aside time each day to indulge in something that brings you joy, alongside time to focus on what gives you purpose. Over time, this habit of giving space to both productivity and release can help to nurture a sustainable, harmonious approach to life.

## Embracing the Imperfections of Our Nature

Being alone with ourselves also requires acceptance. Sometimes, we’ll fall short of our own expectations; we’ll indulge in too many episodes, get lost in daydreams, or push off tasks until the last moment. But rather than resist or resent these tendencies, we can approach them with kindness. Every moment of “wasted” time is a reminder that we are human, that we’re allowed to seek comfort and joy, and that we are more than our productivity.

This compassion for our imperfections is what turns alone time into a space for growth. By embracing the parts of ourselves that are playful, dreamy, or even lazy, we give them room to coexist with the more disciplined and ambitious parts. The beauty of solitude lies in this acceptance of the whole self — not just the part that achieves but the part that rests, explores, and simply exists.

## Redefining Success in the Quiet

When we are alone, the world’s definitions of success fade away, and we have the chance to shape our own. Success doesn’t have to mean constant achievement; it can mean creating something beautiful, exploring our passions, or simply being at peace. Solitude allows us to reflect on what truly matters, what makes us feel alive, and what brings us contentment in a way that external accolades cannot.

So, the next time you find yourself alone, free from the weight of expectations, pause. Let the quiet moments reveal who you are beneath the layers of roles and responsibilities. Let yourself indulge, create, and reflect without guilt. In these moments, you might just find that the most profound achievements are the ones that bring you closer to yourself, reminding you that solitude is not an empty space to be filled, but a canvas on which to paint your own definition of a fulfilling life.

It is an advanced Artificial Intelligence or AI system designed to understand, analyse and generate human like text. LLMs use deep learning techniques, particularly transform architectures, to process information and predict the most probable next word in a given sequence, allowing them to produce coherent and contextually relevant responses.

#### Common Applications of LLMs are:

- **Text Generation** - Creating articles, stories, and other forms of written content.

## How will you identify LLM

When you know their key characteristics, right? So, here are some important characteristics of LLMs:

**Large-Scale Training**: LLMs are large because they are trained on massive datasets of text, such as books and articles from the internet, allowing them to learn grammar, facts and reasoning skills.

**Transformer Architecture**: Many modern LLMs are built on transformer architectures, which use self attention mechanisms to process entire text sequences in parallel, significantly reducing training time compared to older models.

**Natural Language Processing or NLP**: LLMs are a key component of NLP, enabling them to understand the complexities and nuances of human language.

**Predictive Capabilities**: By learning patterns and context from their training data, LLMs can predict the next word in a sentence, which is fundamental to their ability to generate human-like text.

## Local LLM:

A local LLM is a language model that runs directly on you device, rather than in the cloud. You download the model weights and inference code and run everything locally — on your PC, laptop or even a phone (if it is small enough).

### Benefits of Local LLMs

Privacy is maintained, your data stays on your device and not sent to a server.

No internet is required to run it.

Cost is in our control because there is no API costs or subscriptions.

Customization is your hand, you can fine-tune or modify the model yourself.

It has some downsides as well:

Hardware demands is requirement based on large models, we need lots of RAM/VRAM to run it.

To run a local LLM you need the technical knowledge behind it.

It can be slow even when the PC is on lower processing power.

Few examples of Local LLM are like Mistral 7B, LLaMA 3, Phi-3, TinyLLaMA.

Tools like Ollama, LM Studio, Text Generation WebUI or GPT4All are available for you to run these locally easily.

It is a lightweight application and a command-line tool that:

## Postman

Postman is a popular software tool used by developers to build, test and manage APIs(Application Programming Interfaces).

How does Postman solves the problem of testing API:

It helps you send request to APIs (like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and view the responses.

You can test your API endpoints easily without writing code.

We can organise API requests into collections to keep things neat.

Postman automates API testing with Scripts and Workflows.

We can collaborate with teams by sharing API collections and documentation.

And it also generate API documentation automatically.

Postman is generally used by Backend Developers for testing RESTful or GraphQL APIs. QA engineers use it for API testing. DevOps teams use it to manage API deployments. Anyone working with APIs who wants easier way to interact with them can use Postman.

## Auth or Authentication

Auth is short for Authentication, and it is a fundamental concept in computing and security. It refers to verifying the identity of a user, system, or application before granting access to something like a website, an API, or a database.

Authentication asks who are you to give access to the authorised users whom it belongs to.

#### Authentication involves lot of concepts:

Username and Password

API Keys

Tokens (JWT, OAuth)

Bio-metrics (fingerprint, face scan)

Multi-factor authentication (MFA)

There are two different concepts: Authentication and Authorisation

Authentication(Auth) verifies who you are

Authorisation(AuthZ) verifies what you are allowed to do after you are authenticated

To understand the above concept in a better way, assume you are entering a building, where

Auth is showing your ID at the door to enter.

AuthZ is your being allowed into certain rooms of the building.

## Common Types of Auth are:

Basic Auth: Sends username and password in each request(encoded, not encrypted)

API Key: A token(string type) included in the request header or URL to identify the client.

Bearer Token or JWT(JSON Web Token): It a signed token that carries user identity and permissions

OAuth 2.0: It is a secure and delegated authentication ( and used by Google, Facebook, etc.)

Session-based Auth: It works like when user logs in, then server creates session and send session cookie.

SSO(Single Sign-On): It is One login grants access to multiple services (e.g., Google login for many apps).

Pass an API Key

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Depends
import ollama
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

# Using 5, it will limit of the given API key, after that it will not be used. It is working like a credit here.
API_KEYS_CREDITS = {os.getenv("API_KEY"): 5}

app = FastAPI()

def verify_api_key(x_api_key: str = Header(None)):

    # If there is no API key is given, then the credit will be 0
    credits = API_KEYS_CREDITS.get(x_api_key, 0)
    if credits <=0:
        raise HTTPException(status_code = 401, detail = "Invalid API Key, or your credits are over.")

    return x_api_key

@app.post("/generate")
def generate(prompt: str, x_api_key : str = Depends(verify_api_key)):
    API_KEYS_CREDITS[x_api_key] -=1
    response = ollama.chat(model="gemma3:270m", messages=[{"role" : "user", "content": prompt }])
    return {"response": response["message"]["content"]}

```

Feelings Are Just the Growth of Unthought Particles: Understanding the Intersection of Emotion, Thought, and Reality

In the intricate dance between consciousness and existence, feelings emerge as a powerful force, born from the depths of our unconscious mind. They are the unthought particles that shape our emotional landscapes, often appearing unbidden and unexamined. In contrast, thinking — a conscious act of decision-making — arises from the interplay of awareness and reflection. Together, these dimensions of the human experience provide insight into how we navigate the complexities of reality and truth.

In the intricate dance between consciousness and existence, feelings emerge as a powerful force, born from the depths of our unconscious mind. They are the unthought particles that shape our emotional landscapes, often appearing unbidden and unexamined. In contrast, thinking — a conscious act of decision-making — arises from the interplay of awareness and reflection. Together, these dimensions of the human experience provide insight into how we navigate the complexities of reality and truth.

The Nature of Feelings: A Journey Beyond Words
Feelings, as Friedrich Nietzsche once described, are the “shadows of our deeper selves.” They are raw, instinctual responses, emerging from experiences we may not yet fully understand. Unlike thoughts, which are deliberate and structured, feelings are fluid and intuitive. They flow freely, influenced by memories, sensations, and unconscious processes that have yet to be fully articulated.

Carl Jung, in his exploration of the psyche, saw feelings as “compensations” to rational thought — an attempt by the unconscious mind to balance the rational rigidity of our conscious decisions. In this sense, feelings are like unthought particles, seeking expression through symbols and emotions, shaping our subjective realities.

## Thinking: The Conscious Decision of the Mind

Thinking, on the other hand, is a conscious act, rooted in awareness and intention. It allows us to reflect, reason, and analyze, helping us navigate the complexities of life with clarity. However, as Søren Kierkegaard emphasized, “Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.” Thinking, therefore, serves as a bridge between past experiences and future possibilities — an active process where decisions take shape.

In the modern context, mindfulness and critical thinking are increasingly valued as tools to sharpen this process. These practices enable us to explore not just what is convenient or culturally accepted, but what is genuinely authentic and aligned with our true selves.

## Truth Beyond Thought: Reality versus Perception

Often, we confuse what we think is correct with what is truly real. The philosopher John Dewey asserted, “We do not learn from experience… we learn from reflecting on experience.” This distinction is crucial in understanding that thoughts are subjective interpretations of reality, whereas truth exists independently of our perception.

Truth, in its essence, lies beyond the boundaries of subjective thought. It is grounded in experience, evidence, and a deeper understanding of the world. When we prioritize reality over thought, we become more attuned to the subtleties of existence — those moments where feeling and thinking converge to offer insights that words alone cannot capture.

## Living in Alignment with Reality

To live authentically, we must embrace both our feelings and our thoughts, but with a mindful awareness of where they take us. When emotions are allowed to flow freely, yet are tempered by thoughtful reflection, we cultivate a balanced understanding of self and reality. Emotions guide us toward deeper truths, while critical thinking provides the framework for navigating those truths effectively.

Martin Heidegger spoke of “being-in-the-world,” where existence and reality are intertwined. In this state of being, we move beyond dualistic thinking — seeing feelings and thoughts not as separate, but as components of a whole, working in harmony to reveal deeper insights.

## Conclusion

Feelings, as the unthought particles of our unconscious, offer glimpses into experiences we may not yet fully comprehend. Meanwhile, thinking emerges as the conscious process of understanding and shaping our reality. When these aspects are united — when we let our emotions flow while using our minds to reflect and refine — we begin to grasp not just what we feel or think, but what truly is. By grounding ourselves in truth beyond subjective perception, we create a space for authenticity, growth, and deeper understanding of the world around us.

You end up with many unfinished projects and no clear progress.

So, what’s the solution to this rabbit hole?

Before starting anything new, ask yourself:

- Why do I want to do this?
- What will I gain from it?
- How much time do I need to dedicate to reach a certain level?
- What will I lose if I quit halfway?

Only when you can clearly answer these questions can you confidently invest your time. Remember, time is your most valuable resource. The goal is not just to learn, but to learn deeply enough to apply that knowledge — especially in interviews or real-world situations.

That’s how you break the loop: by setting clear priorities and holding yourself accountable. That’s the real solution.

## Embracing Change in College

In college, I encountered an environment that encouraged exploration and personal growth. The diverse range of people I met prompted me to reflect on my introverted nature. I began to realize that while I could still communicate as an introvert, I could also cultivate traits of modesty and humility that my friends noticed in me after we reconnected following a long separation. This change in my personality was not just about being more open; it was about redefining my approach to life and learning.

As I navigated through college, I found myself diving deeper into readings and exploring philosophical ideas. I became more intentional about my activities, seeking out meaning in everything I did. No longer did I engage in activities that felt meaningless; instead, I sought purpose in my studies, physical activities, and personal development.

## From Multitasking to Meaningful Engagement

In high school, I often found myself multitasking, dabbling in various interests without any real commitment. I would jump from one subject to another, learning just enough to enjoy the moment but never truly mastering any of them. This scattered approach left me feeling like a “jack of all trades, master of none.” I realized that this lack of focus was not fulfilling, and I wanted to change that.

So, I made a conscious decision to adopt a more structured, goal-oriented mindset. I began setting specific plans and objectives for my life, recognizing that meaningful decisions required intention. I approached my college studies with a newfound dedication, prioritizing my education and actively seeking knowledge in a more disciplined manner.

I set aside time for studying for exams, learning new skills, running, and walking — all with the understanding that these activities contributed to my growth and well-being. This shift from a haphazard learning style to a more organized approach empowered me to take control of my education and personal development.

As I delved deeper into my studies, I also embraced critical thinking. I started to question the purpose of life and the meaning behind everything I engaged in. Why do we learn? What is the significance of our actions? By contemplating these questions, I found a greater appreciation for knowledge, even when it was challenging or boring.

This critical exploration extended beyond the classroom. I sought to understand the world around me, diving into philosophy, psychology, and various subjects that piqued my interest. I developed a habit of critically examining ideas and theories, challenging myself to think deeply about what I encountered. This not only enriched my understanding of various topics but also helped me appreciate the complexity of life itself.

## A New Perspective on Life

Now, I approach life with a sense of purpose that I lacked before. My experiences in college have taught me that meaningful engagement and intentionality can lead to personal fulfillment. I am no longer simply going through the motions; instead, I seek to understand the “why” behind my actions, striving to make informed decisions that align with my goals.

I’ve learned to embrace my introverted nature while also allowing myself to grow and evolve. I can engage in discussions and express my thoughts without feeling overwhelmed. The modesty and submissiveness that my friends noticed in me are now strengths that help me connect with others in a more meaningful way.

## Conclusion
